Anthropic is offering U.S. K-12 (kindergarten through high school) teachers free access to paid Claude AI features. This initiative is part of a brand-new "Claude for Teachers" program.

"Claude for Teachers" enables U.S. educators to use Anthropic's paid AI features at no cost

Anthropic announced a brand-new "Claude for Teachers" initiative on Tuesday, which includes a suite of Claude skills designed specifically for education.

Anthropic stated: "Upon verification, U.S. K-12 educators will be able to use Claude for Teachers with the Learning Commons connector, along with a set of teaching skills tailored to learning science."

"These skills were developed jointly by Anthropic and Learning Commons, designed around the tasks that teachers tell us matter most to their work. We have evaluated the skills to ensure rigor, instructional alignment, and classroom practicality, and refined them based on early input from frontline teachers (including those at schools such as Prospect Schools in Brooklyn)."

Claude for Teachers includes access to Claude Cowork and Claude Code, enabling educators to use Anthropic's latest AI technology. The company has also recently published an implementation guide for educators interested in using AI in the classroom.

Anthropic said the new "Claude for Teachers" program is designed for individual educators. The AI company also noted that it is developing "solutions designed for schools and districts," to be launched later.

This promotion includes one year of free access to the paid version of Claude. Eligible teachers may apply by June 30, 2027, to receive this benefit.

To learn more about Anthropic's new "Claude for Teachers" program, please visit this link. OpenAI also launched a similar "ChatGPT for Teachers" last November, which is currently available to eligible educators as well.
